Anya: Quick share — ran a targeted perf sweep across Llama-2-13B, Mistral-7B, and Qwen-7B for mixed-precision profiles. Found a surprising regression when FP8 calibration is applied with our aggressive kernel selector.

Anya: TL;DR numbers from the local rig (A100):
- Llama-2-13B fp8+kernel-heuristic: 860 tok/s (baseline int8: 820 tok/s)
- Mistral-7B fp8: 920 tok/s (int8: 900 tok/s)
- Qwen-7B fp8 on kernel-X: 610 tok/s (int8 on kernel-Y: 710 tok/s)

Anya: Qwen is the oddball — fp8 calibration made kernel-X slower than int8 kernel-Y. Logs point at KV cache miss spikes at sequence lengths >512. Full command I used: ```rdw-profile --model qwen-7b --quant fp8 --kernels auto --seq-len 1024 --batch 4 --runs 30```

Devon: Nice data. Could be selector picking a kernel optimized for shorter prefixes (better matmul fusion) but that kernel doesn't do well with the KV copy pattern Qwen uses. The KV cache memcpy+transposes are expensive on that codepath.

Devon: Two quick mitigations to try: 1) add hysteresis to kernel selector so we don't flip on small perf deltas, 2) route seq_len>512 Qwen requests to the int8 kernel as fallback until we track down calibration mismatch.

Matt: Confirming — I repro'd the KV thrash locally. When the selector flips to kernel-X, we see KV_cache_hit_rate drop from ~0.98 -> ~0.75 for warm prefixes. That causes cascade of extra KV materialization and stalls batching.

Matt: Profiling snippet (simplified): ```KV_copy_ms: kernel-X=12.4, kernel-Y=3.1; Matmul_ms: kernel-X=8.7, kernel-Y=9.2; overall token_ms: kernel-X=1.64, kernel-Y=1.42```

Sara: Interesting — I recently updated the fp8 calibration script to use a different bias correction for Qwen activations (to reduce hallucination in evals). That tweak could change the numerical pattern enough that our kernel micro-optimizations behave differently.

Sara: If calibration shifts the activation distribution, the quantized GEMM tiling assumptions might be violated and lead to worse memory access. We should add a quick per-model calibration fingerprint to the profile metadata so selector can prefer compatible kernels.

Anya: Agreed. Proposed short action list:
- Add a per-model calibration hash to the quant profile artifact (so kernel selector only picks kernels that previously ran with the same calib)
- Add seq_len-based routing rule for Qwen to prefer int8 past 512 until we fix kernel-X KV copy path
- Add 10% hysteresis threshold to kernel selection to avoid flip-flop during small perf variance
- Run a microbenchmark for KV copy paths across kernels (small memcopy/transposes) and add to our perf-suite

Devon: I'll put up a tiny PR to implement hysteresis + selector metadata check. For the routing rule we can plumb a policy: model_match && seq_len>512 -> prefer kernel-Y.

Matt: I'll generate the KV microbench and attach results to the PR. Matt: quick FYI numbers after forcing fallback: Qwen int8 fallback -> stable 720 tok/s and KV_hit_rate back to 0.97.

perf-bot: CI-benchmark: qwen-7b fp8 kernel-X (master): 605 tok/s → with hysteresis patch candidate: 718 tok/s (warm run) — preliminary, still flaky on p3 runs. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

Sara: For longer term: add calibration-aware kernel costs into the kernel scoring function (i.e., score = perf_estimate * compatibility_weight(calib_hash)). That way small calibration tweaks won't silently force a slower codepath.

Anya: Good plan. Can we keep this thread as the coordination space? I'll update the shared spreadsheet with the numbers and link the PRs. @Devon @Matt please drop the PR links here when ready.

Devon: Will do. Working on the PR now.

Matt: Microbench attached to my fork, will link once CI completes.

Sara: I'll add the calibration fingerprinting to the quant pipeline; should be low-effort.

Anya: Thanks everyone — goal is to have a safe fallback in prod for Qwen within 48h and long-term selector change in next sprint. :rocket:
